--- title: "Visualizing trends and time series" subtitle: "
36-315: Statistical Graphics and Visualization, Summer 2026" footer: "[36-315-summer26.netlify.app](https://36-315-summer26.netlify.app)" format: revealjs: embed-resources: true height: 900 width: 1600 theme: theme.scss smaller: true slide-number: c/t linestretch: 1.4 code-line-numbers: false html-math-method: method: mathjax url: "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mathjax@3/es5/tex-mml-chtml.js" --- ## Trend and time series data > A **time series** is a sequence of data points indexed, listed, or graphed in chronological order. --- Wikipedia
. . . Main topic ::: {.panel-tabset} ## Time series analysis * What already happened? * Extract meaningful statistics and other characteristics of the data ## **Time series forecasting** * What will happen in the future? * Predict future values based on previously observed values ::: ## Longitudinal data and time series structure * Consider a *single observation* measured across time * Time series data usually has the following structure: | Variable | $T_1$ | $T_2$ | $\dots$ | $T_J$ | | ---------- | -------- | -------- | -------- | -------- | | $X_1$ | $x_{11}$ | $x_{12}$ | $\dots$ | $x_{1J}$ | | $X_2$ | $x_{21}$ | $x_{22}$ | $\dots$ | $x_{2J}$ | | $\vdots$ | $\vdots$ | $\vdots$ | $\dots$ | $\vdots$ | | $X_P$ | $x_{P1}$ | $x_{P2}$ | $\dots$ | $x_{PJ}$ | * With $N$ observations, there are $N$ of these matrices * Time intervals may be regularly or irregularly spaced ## Example: statistics PhDs over time ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} library(tidyverse) theme_set(theme_light()) stats_phd <- read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qntkhvn/36-315-summer26/refs/heads/master/data/stats-phd.csv") head(stats_phd) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 6 × 5 broad_field major_field field year n_phds 1 Life sciences Biological and biomedica… Biom… 2008 122 2 Mathematics and computer sciences Mathematics and statisti… Stat… 2008 303 3 Mathematics and computer sciences Mathematics and statisti… Math… 2008 140 4 Mathematics and computer sciences Mathematics and statisti… Math… 2008 63 5 Psychology and social sciences Other social sciences Stat… 2008 20 6 Education Education research Educ… 2008 66 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} stats_phd_year <- stats_phd |> group_by(year) |> summarize(n_phds = sum(n_phds)) head(stats_phd_year) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 6 × 2 year n_phds 1 2008 870 2 2009 922 3 2010 896 4 2011 885 5 2012 1020 6 2013 1066 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: ## Time series plot Scatterplot with `n_phds` on the y-axis and `year` on the x-axis + Add line to emphasize order + Manually set x-axis breaks to show every year ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="true"} stats_phd_year |> ggplot(aes(x = year, y = n_phds)) + geom_point() + geom_line() + scale_x_continuous(breaks = unique(stats_phd_year$year), labels = unique(stats_phd_year$year)) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture12_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-6-1.png){fig-align='center' width=1152} ::: ::: ## Drop points to emphasize trend ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="true"} stats_phd_year |> ggplot(aes(x = year, y = n_phds)) + geom_line() + scale_x_continuous(breaks = unique(stats_phd_year$year), labels = unique(stats_phd_year$year)) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture12_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-7-1.png){fig-align='center' width=1152} ::: ::: ## Fill area under the line ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="true"} stats_phd_year |> ggplot(aes(x = year, y = n_phds)) + geom_area(fill = "cyan") + scale_x_continuous(breaks = unique(stats_phd_year$year), labels = unique(stats_phd_year$year)) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture12_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-8-1.png){fig-align='center' width=1152} ::: ::: ## Plotting multiple time series: use lines with colors ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="true"} stats_phd |> ggplot(aes(x = year, y = n_phds, color = field)) + geom_line() + scale_x_continuous(breaks = unique(stats_phd$year), labels = unique(stats_phd$year)) ``` ::: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture12_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-10-1.png){fig-align='center' width=1536} ::: ::: :::aside Also known as a spaghetti plot ::: ## Highlight specific lines ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="true"} stats_phd |> filter(!(field %in% c("Biometrics and biostatistics", "Statistics (mathematics)"))) |> ggplot() + geom_line(aes(x = year, y = n_phds, group = field), color = "gray", linewidth = 1, alpha = 0.5) + geom_line(data = filter(stats_phd, field %in% c("Biometrics and biostatistics", "Statistics (mathematics)")), aes(x = year, y = n_phds, color = field), linewidth = 1.5, alpha = 1) + scale_x_continuous(breaks = unique(stats_phd$year), labels = unique(stats_phd$year)) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture12_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-11-1.png){fig-align='center' width=1152} ::: ::: ## Other packages to check out * [`gghighlight`](https://yutannihilation.github.io/gghighlight/) * [`geomtextpath`](https://allancameron.github.io/geomtextpath/) * [`ggrepel`](https://ggrepel.slowkow.com/articles/examples.html) ## Stacked area charts ::: columns ::: {.column}
![](https://meghan.rbind.io/blog/2021-07-20-alternatives-to-simple-color-legends-in-ggplot2/featured.png)
::: ::: {.column}

![](../images/tiers.png)
::: ::: ## Characteristics of time series * **Trends**: Does the variable increase or decrease over time, on average? * **Seasonality**: Are there changes in the variable that regularly happen (e.g., every winter, every hour, etc.)? * **Noise**: Variation in the variable beyond average trends and seasonality ## Moving average * Moving/rolling averages are a starting point for visualizing how a trend changes over time * Intuition * Divide the data into small subsets ("windows") * Compute the average within each window * Connect the averages together to make a trend line * This is sometimes called a simple moving average * Have we seen this before? ## {-} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture12_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-18-1.png){fig-align='center' width=960} ::: ::: ## Computing a moving average Formally, a moving average can be written as $$\mu_k = \frac{1}{h}\sum_{t=k - h + 1}^k X_t$$ * Large $h$: smooth line; captures global trends * Small $h$: jagged/volatile line; captures local trends ## Time series visualization example Data: Mauna Loa monthly atmospheric $\text{CO}_2$ concentration 1959 to 1997 ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="true"} co2 <- read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qntkhvn/36-315-summer26/refs/heads/master/data/co2.csv") co2 |> ggplot(aes(x = obs_date, y = co2_val)) + geom_line() + labs(x = "Time index", y = "CO2 (ppm)") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture12_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-20-1.png){fig-align='center' width=960} ::: ::: ## Use [`ggseas`](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/ggseas/vignettes/ggseas.html) package to plot moving averages ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="true"} library(ggseas) co2 |> ggplot(aes(x = obs_date, y = co2_val)) + geom_line(color = "red") + stat_rollapplyr(width = 12, align = "right") + labs(x = "Year", y = "CO2 (ppm)", title = "Width = 12") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture12_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-21-1.png){fig-align='center' width=960} ::: ::: ## Moving window * Setting `width = 12` and `align = "right"` means for each point, plot the average of a **moving window** consisting of that point and the 11 points behind it * Since this is monthly data, this is the average of a year’s worth of data * Note that there is no trend line for the first 11 points on the left-hand side of the graph * Choose a `width` value that is "just right" * Want the trend to be smooth enough, but also don’t want to deviate from the data too much ## Moving window ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture12_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-22-1.png){fig-align='center' width=960} ::: ::: ## Moving window ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture12_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-23-1.png){fig-align='center' width=960} ::: ::: ## Other moving averages * **Cumulative moving average**: The average at time $k$ is the average of all points at and before $k$. Mathematically: $$\mu_k^{\textsf{(CMA)}} = \frac{1}{k} \sum_{t=1}^k X_t$$ . . . * **Weighted moving average**: Same as simple moving average, but different measurements get different weights for the average. $$\mu_k^{\textsf{(WMA)}} = \frac{\sum_{t=k - h + 1}^k X_t \cdot w_t}{ \sum_{t=k - h + 1}^k w_t}$$ ## Lags * Time series data are not independent and identically distributed (iid) * Example: today's temperature is correlated with yesterday's temperature . . . * **Lags**: a time offset used to compare observations separated by a fixed number of time steps * Lag 1: compare $X_t$ with $X_{t - 1}$ * Lag 2: compare $X_t$ with $X_{t - 2}$ * and so on... . . . * Given time measurements $(X_1, X_2, X_3, X_4, X_5)$ * Lag 1 compares $(X_2, X_3, X_4, X_5)$ with $(X_1, X_2, X_3, X_4)$ * Lag 2 compares $(X_3, X_4, X_5)$ vs $(X_1, X_2, X_3)$. ## Autocorrelation * **Autocorrelation**: correlation between a time series and a lagged version of itself . . . * Define $r_{\ell}$ as the correlation between a time series and lag $\ell$ of that time series * Lag 1: $r_1$ is correlation between $(X_2, X_3, X_4, X_5)$ and $(X_1,X_2,X_3,X_4)$ * Lag 2: $r_2$ is correlation between $(X_3, X_4, X_5)$ and $(X_1,X_2,X_3)$ * and so on... . . . * Common diagnostic: plot $\ell$ on x-axis, $r_{\ell}$ on y-axis * Reveals if correlations are significantly large/small for certain lags ## Autocorrelation plots ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="true"} library(ggfortify) auto_corr <- acf(co2$co2_val, plot = FALSE) autoplot(auto_corr) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture12_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-24-1.png){fig-align='center' width=960} ::: ::: ## Autocorrelation plots and seasonality * With strong global trends, autocorrelations will be very positive * Visualize autocorrelations after removing the global trend ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="true"} wid12 <- co2 |> ggplot(aes(x = obs_date, y = co2_val)) + geom_line(color="red") + stat_rollapplyr(width = 12, align = "right") + labs(x = "Year", y = "CO2 (ppm)") co2 <- co2 |> mutate(moving_avg = zoo::rollapply(co2_val, width = 12, FUN = "mean", align = "right", fill = NA), resid = co2_val - moving_avg) resid_plot <- co2 |> ggplot(aes(x = obs_date, y = resid)) + geom_line() + labs(x = "Year", y = "Residuals of CO2 (ppm)") library(patchwork) wid12 + resid_plot ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture12_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-25-1.png){fig-align='center' width=960} ::: ::: ## Autocorrelation plots and seasonality ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="true"} # ACF of the residuals (except the first 11 points, which are NA) autoplot(acf(tail(co2$resid, -11), plot = FALSE)) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture12_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-26-1.png){fig-align='center' width=960} ::: ::: ## Seasonal decomposition * STL decomposition (**S**easonal decomposition of **T**ime series by **L**oess) * Break down a time series into three characteristics: **trend**, **seasonality**, **noise** . . . * Use `ggsdc()` (from [`ggseas`](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/ggseas/vignettes/ggseas.html)) to visualize seasonal decomposition * `observed`: original time series * `trend`: loess curve; global trend * `seasonality`: another loess curve as the seasonality (observed - trend) * `irregular`: irregular/residual noise (observed - trend - seasonality) * In other words: `trend` + `seasonality` + `irregular` = `observed` ## Seasonal decomposition ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="true"} co2 |> ggsdc(aes(obs_date, co2_val), frequency = 12, method = "stl", s.window = 12) + geom_line() + labs(x = "Year", y = "CO2 (ppm)") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture12_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-27-1.png){fig-align='center' width=576} ::: :::

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
